t: You're at the site of St Peter le Poer, a parish church that once stood on the west side of Broad Street. It was established before the end of the twelfth century, rebuilt in 1540, and rebuilt again in 1792 by the architect Jesse Gibson, with a circular nave. It was demolished in 1907, so what you're looking at now is where it used to be. Several mathematicians were buried here: Edmund Gunter, who invented Gunter's chain, quadrant and scale, and Henry Gellibrand, who showed that magnetic declination changes over time. Thomas Neale, an English politician, is buried here too.
